subject.title: fix(mcp): standalone apps stop hanging on stalled gateway requests

question: Should a standalone MCP App operation deadline only detach that caller while a runtime-owned catalog refresh continues to completion and warms the shared cache after the final waiter has gone away?
rationale: This is an intentional resource-lifecycle and availability tradeoff, not a mechanical defect: the correct behavior depends on the MCP runtime owner’s intended cache-warming, transport, and cancellation policy.

options.title: Keep runtime-owned cache warming
options.body: Approve the branch’s model: an expired operation stops waiting, while an already-started shared catalog refresh remains owned by the runtime until it completes or the runtime disposes.

options.title: Cancel orphaned refreshes
options.body: Require the branch to abort shared catalog work once its final operation waiter detaches, accepting less cache warming in exchange for tighter resource reclamation.

recommendation.title: Keep runtime-owned cache warming
recommendation.body: Approve the branch’s model: an expired operation stops waiting, while an already-started shared catalog refresh remains owned by the runtime until it completes or the runtime disposes.
